recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant Bundle or HTTP prose; if future work is needed for arbitrary response headers, handle it in the FHIR Extension Pack rather than core.
issue_request: FHIR-5539 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Feed change request from DSTU1 asking to reuse RESTful HTTP status semantics in transaction results instead of relying on older implicit Bundle entry status, resource metadata, and deleted-entry modeling.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly names FHIR-5539. The application appears to be the early 2015 Bundle transaction rework after Connectathon discussion, followed by the March 2015 http-response-header extension commit and the later FHIR-8878 clarification that Bundle.entry.response.status must include at least a three-digit HTTP status code.
additional_context: Bundle is an active normative current-build resource. Current Bundle source requires entry.response for transaction-response and batch-response bundles, defines mandatory Bundle.entry.response.status as starting with a three-digit HTTP code with optional text, and carries Location, ETag, lastModified, and outcome response fields. The RESTful HTTP narrative says batch/transaction response entries contain the HTTP status code and applicable Location and ETag header values. The old http-response-header extension was intentionally removed from core R5 source with other extensions and is present in the FHIR Extension Pack.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because current core source already conveys the FHIR-5539 decision and reintroducing the old core extension would be incorrect for the current build.

related_jiras.note: Published clarification of Bundle.entry.response.status possible values; it supports the current HTTP-code wording but was not decided by this seed audit.
A later history-response status wording issue already represented on the combined branch; it does not change the FHIR-5539 transaction-response conclusion.
